objectives and content
    ObjectivesBy the end of the course students can1) write clear and concise proofs in natural language using various proving techniques such as contradiction, case distinction, induction and double counting.
2) apply definitions of and formally reason about
  a)  functions, relations and orderings
  b) graphs, directed graphs and planar graphs
  c) rooted and unrooted trees
3) identify and reason with various properties of graphs such as Hamiltonian, Eulerian, k-connectivity.
4) apply the basics of combinatorial counting such as counting functions, number of subsets or using the inclusion / exclusion principle
    ContentIn this course we will cover basic discrete mathematical structures that occur in many contexts in computer science. You will learn the basic skills and knowledge to formally reason about these structures. Among others we will cover relations and orderings, counting arguments, and graphs and trees.
